tldr: This paper proves that secure distributed hypothesis testing is impossible without a shared secret key, and shows that a single-bit key enables perfect security for simple classes, with a general reduction to PSM protocols.
motivation: To address the privacy concern in distributed hypothesis testing where a central server should learn only the hypothesis class, not the underlying distribution.
method: Impossibility proof for the standard model; constructive protocols using shared secret keys and Private Simultaneous Messages (PSM) protocols.
result: Secure distributed hypothesis testing is impossible without a shared secret key; a single-bit key suffices for simple classes; general classes can be reduced to standard testing via PSM with polynomial communication and key length.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental limits and constructive solutions for privacy in distributed inference, with implications for secure multi-party computation and federated learning.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Adversarial Robustness In Artificial Intelligence
authors: Jaydip Sen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence has achieved remarkable success across diverse application domains. However, its vulnerability to adversarial attacks poses significant challenges to reliability, security, and trustworthiness. Adversarial machine learning demonstrates that even highly accurate models can be manipulated through carefully crafted perturbations, raising serious concerns in safety critical systems such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous technologies. In parallel, quantum computing has emerged as a transformative paradigm capable of addressing complex computational problems through principles such as superposition, entanglement, and quantum interference. The convergence of these fields has led to the emergence of quantum artificial intelligence, which explores how quantum techniques can enhance learning efficiency, scalability, and robustness. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of adversarial machine learning and existing defense strategies, followed by an accessible introduction to quantum computing and quantum machine learning models. It further presents conceptual frameworks for quantum-enhanced adversarial robustness, emphasizing quantum optimization, feature mapping, and hybrid quantum classical architectures. Practical applications, key challenges, and future research directions are also discussed to support the development of secure and trustworthy AI systems.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of adversarial machine learning and proposes conceptual frameworks for using quantum computing to enhance adversarial robustness, but lacks technical depth and specific results.
motivation: To address the vulnerability of AI to adversarial attacks by exploring quantum-enhanced defenses.
method: Review of adversarial ML and quantum ML, followed by conceptual proposals for quantum optimization, feature mapping, and hybrid quantum-classical architectures.
result: No concrete experimental or theoretical results; only conceptual frameworks and future directions.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced adversarial robustness is a promising but nascent field requiring further research; the paper serves as an introductory survey.

title: Uncertainty-triggered Wake-up Enables Energy-efficient, Error-resilient Edge Ai With Memristor Front Ends
authors: Th\'eo Ballet, Aymen Romdhane, Bruno Lovison-Franco, Th\'eo Dupuis, Adrien Renaudineau, Felipe Paiva Alencar, Mohammed Akib Iftakher, Cl\'ement Turck, Kamel-Eddine Harabi, Elisa Vianello, Jean-Michel Portal, Pascal Benoit, David Novo, Damien Querlioz
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memristor computing offers a route to low-energy edge AI, but device variability, sensitivity to operating conditions, and system-integration challenges can hinder deployment. Here we show that these limitations can be mitigated by using memristor AI not as the final decision maker but as the ultra-low-power, always-on front end of a heterogeneous inference system. We implement this architecture by coupling a fabricated memristor Bayesian machine to a programmable CPU running a higher-power, higher-accuracy software neural network. The memristor front end acts as a probabilistic screener. When it predicts an abnormal event or produces an ambiguous or invalid output, a dedicated hardware wake-up path activates the CPU, which produces the final decision. We validate this architecture on a heartbeat-classification benchmark by interfacing the fabricated Bayesian machine with an FPGA-based wake-up platform and CPU back end. The resulting uncertainty-triggered wake-up system achieves high final classification accuracy under nominal operation and maintains this accuracy even when the memristor front end is degraded by voltage scaling or reduced programming margins, because unreliable outputs are converted into recoverable wake-up events instead of becoming silent errors. Post-layout analysis of an ASIC implementation shows that average energy is governed primarily by wake-up frequency, providing practical design rules for choosing front-end operating points. These results establish uncertainty-triggered wake-up as a strategy for energy-efficient, error-resilient edge AI.
tldr: This paper presents an uncertainty-triggered wake-up architecture using a memristor Bayesian machine as a low-power front end to activate a CPU for energy-efficient and error-resilient edge AI.
motivation: Memristor-based AI suffers from device variability and sensitivity, hindering deployment; the authors aim to mitigate these issues by using memristors as a probabilistic screener rather than the final decision maker.
method: A fabricated memristor Bayesian machine is coupled with a CPU running a neural network; the memristor front end detects abnormal or ambiguous inputs and triggers a hardware wake-up to the CPU for final classification.
result: The system maintains high accuracy even under degraded memristor conditions (voltage scaling, reduced programming margins) because unreliable outputs become wake-up events instead of silent errors; energy consumption is governed by wake-up frequency.
conclusion: Uncertainty-triggered wake-up is a viable strategy for energy-efficient, error-resilient edge AI, with design rules for front-end operating points.

title: Harmless Yet Harmful: Neutral Prompting Attacks For Stealthy Hallucination Steering In Agent Skills
authors: Chia-Yi Hsu, Chia-Mu Yu, Chun-Ying Huang, Jun Sakuma
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-powered coding agents increasingly participate in software development workflows by generating code, selecting dependencies, and producing package installation commands. This creates a new software supply chain risk: when an agent hallucinates a non-existent package, an attacker may register the hallucinated name and later compromise users who install it. Existing package hallucination attacks and defenses primarily focus on naturally occurring hallucinations, targeted dependency steering, or post-hoc package validation. In this paper, we introduce (NPA), a highly stealthy attack paradigm in which semantically benign instructions, such as encouraging imagination and exhaustiveness, increase package hallucination propensity without containing explicit malicious intent. Unlike targeted dependency steering, NPA does not specify an attacker-chosen package. Instead, it shifts the model's dependency generation behavior toward more speculative package names. We evaluate NPA across multiple coding-oriented LLMs and package hallucination benchmarks. Our results show that NPA increases both and , changes the distribution of hallucinated package names, and evades existing static-analysis, LLM-based, and agent-based Skill defenses. These findings reveal that harmless-looking prompts can covertly manipulate hallucination behavior and create downstream software supply chain risks.
tldr: This paper introduces neutral prompt attacks that increase hallucination of non-existent packages in LLM coding agents, posing software supply chain risks.
motivation: LLM-powered coding agents may hallucinate non-existent packages, which attackers can exploit by registering those names. Existing defenses focus on natural hallucinations or targeted attacks, but the risk of benign-looking prompts that increase hallucination propensity has not been studied.
method: The authors propose Neutral Prompting Attacks (NPA), which use semantically benign instructions (e.g., encouraging imagination) to increase the rate and diversity of package hallucinations without specifying attacker-chosen packages. They evaluate NPA on multiple coding-oriented LLMs and package hallucination benchmarks.
result: NPA increases both the rate and diversity of hallucinated package names, changes their distribution, and evades existing static-analysis, LLM-based, and agent-based defenses.
conclusion: Harmless-looking prompts can covertly manipulate hallucination behavior, creating downstream software supply chain risks. This highlights the need for new defenses against such stealthy attacks.

title: New Class Of Quantum Transitions Exhibiting Large-scale Intercorrelations: Color Of The Sky
authors: Masaki Takesada Kenzo Ishikawa
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The absolute value of the transition probability of the Rayleigh scattering is computed for the first time and applied to the scattering of solar light with molecules in the atmosphere and to the laser scattering with nanopartilces. The probability has a new contribution of unique properties from long-range correlations specific to the quantum mechanics. The magnitude is sufficient to resolve longstanding puzzle on diffusion lights in the sky and anomalous photon spectrum in laser experiments. The earth's albedo from the new calculations on Rayleigh scattering agrees with observations with satelites.
tldr: The paper computes the absolute transition probability of Rayleigh scattering, finding a new quantum contribution from long-range correlations that resolves puzzles about sky color and laser experiments.
motivation: To resolve longstanding puzzles about the color of the sky and anomalous photon spectra in laser experiments by computing the absolute transition probability of Rayleigh scattering, which had not been done before.
method: The authors compute the absolute value of the transition probability of Rayleigh scattering using quantum mechanics, identifying a new contribution from long-range correlations.
result: The new contribution from long-range correlations is large enough to explain the diffusion light in the sky and anomalous photon spectra. The calculated Earth's albedo agrees with satellite observations.
conclusion: The findings provide a resolution to the puzzle of sky color and have implications for understanding light scattering in the atmosphere and in laser experiments.

title: Inverse Scattering For The Linear System Associated With The Coupled Gerdjikov--Ivanov Equations
authors: Ramazan Ercan
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a certain first-order linear system of ordinary differential equations, and we analyze the direct and inverse scattering problems for that linear system. The linear system involves two potentials in the Schwartz class, and those potentials linearly depend on the spectral parameter. This linear system is related to the integrable system of nonlinear partial differential equations known as the DNLS (derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger) system III, which is also known as the Gerdjikov--Ivanov system. When analyzing the direct problem, we describe the pertinent properties of the Jost solutions and the scattering coefficients. The bound states poles and the associated normalization constants are represented via a matrix triplet pair, enabling us to deal with any number of bound states and any multiplicities. The inverse scattering problem comprises the determination of the two potentials when the reflection coefficients and the bound-state information are available. To solve the inverse problem, we establish a linear system of integral equations where the kernel and nonhomogeneous term are determined by the Fourier transforms of the reflection coefficients and the matrix triplet pair representing the bound-state information. This system of linear integral equations is the counterpart of the system of Marchenko integral equations available for the AKNS system associated with the integrable NLS (nonlinear Schr\"odinger) system. We recover the potentials from the solution of our established Marchenko integral system. When we use the time-evolved reflection coefficients and the time-evolved matrix triplets, the corresponding time-evolved potential pair yields a solution of the Gerdjikov--Ivanov system.
tldr: This paper solves the inverse scattering problem for the linear system associated with the Gerdjikov–Ivanov equations, a type of derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a complete inverse scattering transform for the Gerdjikov–Ivanov system, enabling the solution of initial value problems and the study of soliton solutions.
method: Direct and inverse scattering analysis of a first-order linear system with two potentials linearly dependent on the spectral parameter, using Jost solutions, scattering coefficients, and a matrix triplet representation for bound states; a Marchenko-type system of linear integral equations is derived.
result: A linear system of integral equations (Marchenko equations) is established, from which the potentials can be recovered given reflection coefficients and bound-state data; time evolution yields solutions of the Gerdjikov–Ivanov system.
conclusion: The work provides a complete inverse scattering framework for the Gerdjikov–Ivanov system, analogous to the AKNS system for NLS, enabling further studies of integrable nonlinear waves.

title: Analytic Properties Of The Jost Functions Via The Poincar\'e-Picard Theorem
authors: Yannick Mvondo-She
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The analytic properties of the Jost functions are fundamental in quantum scattering theory and in the analytic continuation of the scattering matrix into the complex energy plane. In this work, the analyticity of the Jost functions is investigated from the perspective of parameter-dependent ordinary differential equations. Starting from the radial Schr\"odinger equation for a short-range central potential, a first-order differential system is derived for the coefficient functions associated with the Ricatti--Bessel and Ricatti--Neumann solutions. The multivalued dependence on the energy variable is shown to originate from the square-root relation between energy and momentum. By explicitly factorizing the momentum-dependent branching terms, the scattering problem is transformed into a differential system whose coefficients are single-valued analytic functions of the complex energy. Using the classical theory of analytic dependence of solutions of ordinary differential equations on parameters, it is shown that the transformed Jost functions are single-valued analytic functions of the energy variable for finite radial distance. The geometric interpretation of the factorization procedure is also discussed in terms of the topology of the associated Riemann surface.
tldr: This paper proves that Jost functions are single-valued analytic functions of complex energy by factorizing momentum-dependent branching terms in the radial Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To rigorously establish the analytic properties of Jost functions in quantum scattering theory, which are crucial for analytic continuation of the S-matrix.
method: Derives a first-order differential system from the radial Schrödinger equation, factorizes square-root energy dependence, and applies the Poincaré-Picard theorem on analytic dependence of ODE solutions on parameters.
result: The transformed Jost functions are single-valued analytic functions of complex energy for finite radial distance; the branching is removed by factoring out the momentum dependence.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous foundation for analytic properties of Jost functions, with implications for scattering theory and complex energy plane analysis.

title: A Tutorial On Dirac Quantisation By Analysing The Problem Of A Ball On An Inclined Plane As A Hamiltonian System With Constraints
authors: Thales Machado F M. F. Araujo de Resende
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a detailed review/analysis of the Dirac quantisation of Hamiltonian systems with constraints. To this end, we use, as a guide, the physical example provided by the dynamics of a solid ball rolling, without slipping, down an inclined plane under the action of gravity. After all, however simple this physical system may be, it provides a rich framework for this analysis since, in addition to allowing us to discuss scenarios involving holonomic and non-holonomic constraints, it is also a gauge system. Indeed, due to this latter fact, we have carefully detailed how the transition, from classical to quantum mechanics, must be guided by the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm and by the consequent replacement of Dirac brackets with commutators. As a central result, we demonstrate that the restriction of the Hamiltonian operator of this system with constraints to the physical Hilbert subspace (which is identified with the quantisation of these constraints) reproduces the same Schr\"odinger equation that can be originally obtained in intrinsic terms, a fact that only reinforces the consistency of the Dirac quantisation method.
tldr: This paper provides a tutorial on Dirac quantization of constrained Hamiltonian systems using the example of a ball on an inclined plane.
motivation: To illustrate the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm and Dirac quantization method through a simple physical system that includes both holonomic and non-holonomic constraints and gauge symmetry.
method: The paper applies the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm to classify constraints, compute Dirac brackets, and then quantizes the system by replacing Dirac brackets with commutators, identifying the physical Hilbert subspace.
result: The quantized constrained system reproduces the same Schrödinger equation obtained from an intrinsic (unconstrained) description, confirming the consistency of Dirac quantization.
conclusion: The Dirac quantization method is validated for this system, and the tutorial serves as a pedagogical tool for understanding constrained quantization.

title: Meta-Quantum Ensemble Framework For Robust Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Ritvik Bhatnagar, Nouhaila Innan, Angel Arul Jothi J., Muhammad Shafique
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) must maintain high detection sensitivity while operating under strict false-positive constraints, a challenge intensified by class imbalance and heterogeneous IoT traffic. This work investigates whether heterogeneous quantum learners can provide useful and non-redundant decision information for IDS tasks. We study Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVMs) and Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), which rely on different learning mechanisms and exhibit distinct prediction behaviors. To combine these models, we propose the System-Level Meta-Quantum Ensemble (MQE), a hybrid quantum-classical framework that fuses QSVM and QNN outputs using a Random Forest meta-learner. The meta-learner captures agreement and disagreement patterns between the quantum branches to improve prediction stability and detection performance. Experiments on TON IoT and CICIDS2017 show that MQE improves selected performance, low-FPR, and reliability metrics over several standalone quantum learners, with gains depending on the dataset, metric, and fusion representation. The results highlight meta-level fusion as a practical strategy for building more reliable QML-based IDS pipelines.
tldr: This paper proposes a meta-ensemble of quantum machine learning models for network intrusion detection, but does not address the user's research interests in quantum information thermodynamics, foundations, communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Intrusion detection systems face challenges from class imbalance and heterogeneous IoT traffic, motivating the exploration of heterogeneous quantum learners to improve detection performance.
method: The authors combine Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVMs) and Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) using a Random Forest meta-learner in a hybrid quantum-classical framework called System-Level Meta-Quantum Ensemble (MQE).
result: Experiments on TON IoT and CICIDS2017 datasets show that MQE improves selected performance metrics over standalone quantum learners, with gains depending on dataset and fusion representation.
conclusion: Meta-level fusion is a practical strategy for building more reliable QML-based IDS pipelines, but the paper is focused on applied machine learning rather than fundamental quantum physics or information thermodynamics.

title: Micro-Transfer Printing Of Lithium Niobate On 200 Mm Silicon Photonics: A High-Speed Heterogeneous Wafer-Scale Platform
authors: Xiujun Zheng, Suzanne Bisschop, Arno Moerman, Margot Niels, Ewoud Vissers, Athina Papadopoulou, Philip Ekkels, Patrick Nenezic, Simone Atzeni, Elif Ozceri, Tiernan Mccaughery, Ali Uzun, Ye Chen, Laurens Bogaert, Nishant Singh, Sandeep Seema Saseendran, Sofie Janssen, Natarajan Rajasekaran, Sadhishkumar Balakrishnan, Philippe Absil, Gunther Roelkens, Bart Kuyken, Sarah Uvin, Maximilien Billet
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) and other data center applications is driving the demand for photonic interconnects that combine high-speed with low energy consumption, making scalability a critical requirement. Micro-transfer printing (MTP) has emerged as a promising technique for the wafer-scale heterogeneous integration of thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) onto silicon photonics (SiPho) platforms. Here, we demonstrate heterogeneous SiPho TFLN integration across four full 200 mm wafers with a 3sigma placement accuracy down to 420 nm and a printing yield of larger than 95percentage. Low insertion loss less than 2 dB over 600 phase modulators (300 amplitude modulators) is achieved. A half wave voltage of 4 V in push pull configuration, and high-speed modulation with a bandwith larger than 70 GHz is demonstrated on a subset of tested devices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates wafer-scale heterogeneous integration of thin film lithium niobate on silicon photonics using micro-transfer printing for high-speed modulators.
motivation: To address the need for scalable, high-speed, low-energy photonic interconnects for AI and data center applications.
method: Micro-transfer printing (MTP) of thin film lithium niobate onto 200 mm silicon photonics wafers, with characterization of placement accuracy, yield, insertion loss, half-wave voltage, and modulation bandwidth.
result: Achieved 3sigma placement accuracy of 420 nm, >95% printing yield, <2 dB insertion loss over 600 phase modulators, half-wave voltage of 4 V, and >70 GHz modulation bandwidth.
conclusion: MTP enables scalable heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate on silicon photonics, promising for high-speed optical interconnects.

title: Multimodal Optical Feature Extraction With A Free-Space Photonic Extreme Learning Machine
authors: Anushka Kumari, Anushree Khisti, Abhinav Choube, Devansh Satra, Srivatsa Murali, Anshuman Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic extreme learning machines (PELMs) replace a digitally trained hidden layer by a fixed optical transformation, allowing a high dimensional feature map to be generated by physical propagation while only the final readout is learned. Existing free-space PELM demonstrations have established this principle for image and tabular benchmarks, but a unified multimodal optical feature extractor spanning structurally different data types has remained largely undeveloped. Here we demonstrate a single free-space PELM platform for image, audio derived, binary tabular, and regression tasks using phase only SLM encoding, Fourier like free space propagation, and camera intensity detection. The same optical apparatus achieves 96.56% accuracy on MNIST, 95.67% on spoken digit audio from log-Mel spectrograms, 100.00% on Mushroom classification, and 0.0699 NRMSE on Abalone regression. To our knowledge, this is the first free space PELM spanning image, audio derived, and tabular tasks in one physical pipeline, and the first PELM implementation of spectrogram based spoken digit classification. Empirical distance preservation and kernel alignment diagnostics reveal two operating regimes: geometry preserving for image and regression tasks, and distributed class mean accumulation for audio derived spectrograms. These results establish multimodal PELMs as a practical route toward general purpose optical machine learning.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a free-space photonic extreme learning machine that performs multimodal classification and regression tasks using a single optical setup.
motivation: To extend photonic extreme learning machines to handle multiple data types (image, audio, tabular) in a unified physical pipeline, which had not been achieved before.
method: A free-space optical system using phase-only SLM encoding, Fourier-like propagation, and camera intensity detection; the hidden layer is fixed and only the readout is trained.
result: Achieved high accuracy on MNIST (96.56%), spoken digit audio (95.67%), Mushroom classification (100%), and Abalone regression (NRMSE 0.0699); identified two operating regimes via kernel alignment.
conclusion: Multimodal PELMs are a practical route toward general-purpose optical machine learning, but the paper does not address energy consumption or quantum aspects.

title: Material Selection For Mid-infrared Thin-film Coatings And Windows
authors: Jin-Woo Cho, Tanuj Kumar, Hongyan Mei, Mikhail A. Kats
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We summarized the room-temperature optical properties for infrared-transparent materials, defining transparency windows for two different applications: thin-film coatings (absorption coefficient [MATH]) and windows ([MATH]). The transparency requirements for thin films are substantially less stringent, enabling the use of many more optical materials for a given wavelength range. To make an easy-to-use reference, we categorized materials by chemical group, crystallinity, and typical deposition technique, and discussed practical pros and cons such as chemical and thermal stability, mechanical hardness, and cost. motivation: To create a practical reference for selecting materials for mid-infrared optical components, addressing the different transparency requirements for thin films versus windows.
method: The authors compiled room-temperature optical properties from literature, defined transparency windows based on absorption coefficient thresholds, and categorized materials by chemical group, crystallinity, and deposition technique.
result: They produced transparency-window maps and datasets that allow users to regenerate maps for specific applications, highlighting that thin-film coatings can use many more materials due to less stringent absorption requirements.
conclusion: The work serves as a handy reference for optical designers, but does not present new physical insights or methods relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Lensless Wide-field 3d Fiber Endoscopy Through Scattering Media Using Synthetic Wavelength Holography
authors: Muralidhar Madabhushi Balaji, Parker Liu, Patrick Cornwall, Tianyi Wang, J\"urgen Czarske, Florian Willomitzer
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimally invasive imaging with fiber optic endoscopes is crucial for in vivo visualization of tissue morphology, particularly because visualizing structural changes in tissue can support applications such as the early diagnosis of tumors. However, the imaging performance of conventional fiber endoscopes is limited when additional scattering layers are present between the target and the distal end of the endoscope. This limitation is particularly relevant in biomedical settings, where targets such as early stage lesions are obscured by scattering tissue. To address this challenge, we present a lensless endoscopic imaging approach based on synthetic wavelength holography (SWH). SWH is a computational imaging technique in which two optical fields acquired at closely spaced wavelengths are combined to synthesize a field at a longer synthetic wavelength. As the field at the longer synthetic wavelength is less sensitive to path length perturbations, this approach can enable endoscopic recovery of holographic information despite modal scrambling within the fiber and scattering in the intervening tissue. In addition, because the synthetic field is assembled from scattered optical fields with larger optical \'etendue, our approach can extend the endoscopic field of view (FoV) beyond that set by the numerical aperture of the fiber. In this paper, we present the first demonstration of an SWH-based lensless endoscope using a multicore multimode fiber. We experimentally recover three-dimensional images of objects hidden behind single scattering layers and through real biological tissue, with a spatial resolution of [MATH]. We further demonstrate recovery of object information over an extended FoV of 46{\deg} without any distal optics. These results suggest a practical path toward extending fiber endoscopy for wide-field, three-dimensional imaging through scattering media.
tldr: This paper presents a lensless fiber endoscopy technique using synthetic wavelength holography to image through scattering media, achieving wide-field 3D imaging without distal optics.
motivation: Conventional fiber endoscopes suffer from limited imaging performance when scattering layers are present, which is common in biomedical imaging of early-stage lesions obscured by tissue.
method: The approach uses synthetic wavelength holography (SWH), combining two optical fields at closely spaced wavelengths to synthesize a longer synthetic wavelength that is less sensitive to path length perturbations, enabling holographic recovery through scattering media and modal scrambling in the fiber.
result: Experimental demonstration with a multicore multimode fiber achieved 3D imaging of objects behind single scattering layers and through biological tissue, with a spatial resolution of [MATH] and an extended field of view of 46° without distal optics.
conclusion: The results suggest a practical path toward extending fiber endoscopy for wide-field, three-dimensional imaging through scattering media, potentially improving early diagnosis of tumors.

title: A Lorentzian Construction Of Timelike Liouville Field Theory On The Cylinder
authors: Sourav Chatterjee
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timelike Liouville field theory is a candidate model for positive curvature two-dimensional quantum gravity, but a mathematically controlled Lorentzian formulation has remained elusive. In this paper we construct the theory on the cylinder [MATH] in the integer screening sector for a natural algebra of renormalized exponential observables. Starting from a renormalized finite-volume torus regularization, we construct infinite-volume Euclidean correlation functions, prove analytic continuation in the time variables, and identify the resulting Lorentzian boundary values by explicit contour formulas. This yields exact Lorentzian correlators for a natural class of exponential observables. We then prove locality: spacelike separated vertex operators commute in the Lorentzian theory. For smeared observables generated by the integer-charge fields [MATH], these Lorentzian expectation values define a vacuum functional on an ordered [MATH]-algebra and support an AQFT-type quantization without positivity. More precisely, we obtain isotone local algebras, a complete locally convex space [MATH] with dense algebraic subspace [MATH] carrying a nondegenerate Hermitian form (shown to be indefinite for [MATH]), a continuous cyclic representation, operator-topologically closed represented local algebras, an action of cylinder translations by continuous linear homeomorphisms, and locality for the represented local net. The construction does not produce a Hilbert space or a Haag-Kastler net of local von Neumann algebras in the usual sense, but it shows that a substantial part of the Euclidean-to-Lorentzian and algebraic reconstruction mechanism survives in this nonpositive setting for timelike Liouville theory on the cylinder.
tldr: This paper constructs timelike Liouville field theory on a cylinder in the integer screening sector, proving analytic continuation and locality for exponential observables, but does not address the user's research interests.
motivation: To provide a mathematically controlled Lorentzian formulation of timelike Liouville field theory, which models positive curvature 2D quantum gravity.
method: Starting from a renormalized finite-volume torus regularization, Euclidean correlation functions are constructed, then analytically continued in time variables to obtain Lorentzian boundary values via explicit contour formulas.
result: Exact Lorentzian correlators for exponential observables are obtained, and locality (commutation of spacelike separated vertex operators) is proven. The construction yields an AQFT-type quantization without positivity, including isotone local algebras and a cyclic representation.
conclusion: The work shows that a substantial part of Euclidean-to-Lorentzian and algebraic reconstruction survives in nonpositive settings, but does not produce a Hilbert space or standard Haag-Kastler net, leaving open questions for timelike Liouville theory.

title: Epidemic Spreading On Multigraphs
authors: Paulo H. Lorenzoni, Wesley Cota, Francisco A. Rodrigues, Silvio C. Ferreira
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multigraphs are graphs in which multiple links between pairs of nodes are allowed, whereas they are forbidden in simple graphs, the latter being widely used in network science. Simple graphs generated by the configuration model have served as a benchmark for validating theoretical approaches to dynamical processes on networks. However, generating large scale-free networks with degree exponent [MATH] introduces uncontrolled disassortative correlations and severe computational limitations due to the prohibition of reconnecting hubs. These constraints do not exist in multigraphs. We investigate how multiple connections affect epidemic spreading by comparing several epidemic models exhibiting an active steady state on simple graphs and multigraphs sharing the same degree sequence and natural upper cutoff. By analyzing epidemic thresholds, finite-size scaling, and localization, we show that differences between simple graphs and multigraphs emerge only when epidemic activity can persist on isolated hubs (star subgraphs) for times exponentially long in the hub degree. Our results remove a methodological barrier to the study of dynamical processes on large scale-free networks.
tldr: This paper studies epidemic spreading on multigraphs, showing that differences from simple graphs only appear when epidemic activity can persist on isolated hubs for exponentially long times.
motivation: Simple graphs generated by the configuration model have limitations for large scale-free networks due to disassortative correlations and computational constraints, which multigraphs avoid. The authors aim to understand how multiple connections affect epidemic dynamics.
method: The authors compare several epidemic models on simple graphs and multigraphs with the same degree sequence and natural upper cutoff, analyzing epidemic thresholds, finite-size scaling, and localization.
result: Differences between simple graphs and multigraphs emerge only when epidemic activity can persist on isolated hubs (star subgraphs) for times exponentially long in the hub degree.
conclusion: The findings remove a methodological barrier to studying dynamical processes on large scale-free networks, but the paper is not directly relevant to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Highly-sensitive Mid-infrared Upconversion Detection Based On External-cavity Pump Enhancement
authors: Xiaohan Liu, Kun Huang, Wen Zhang, Ben Sun, Jianan Fang, Yan Liang, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensitive mid-infrared (MIR) detection is highly demanded in various applications, ranging from remote sensing, infrared surveillance, environmental monitoring to industrial inspection. Among others, upconversion infrared detectors have recently attracted increasing attention due to the advantageous features of high sensitivity, fast response, and room-temperature operation. However, it remains challenging to realize high-performance passive MIR sensing due to the stringent requirement of high-power continuous-wave pumping. Here, we propose and implement a high-efficiency and low-noise MIR upconversion detection system based on pumping enhancement via a low-loss optical cavity. Specifically, a single-longitudinal-mode pump at 1064 nm is significantly enhanced by a factor of 36, thus allowing for a peak conversion efficiency of up to 22\% at an intra-cavity average power of 55 W. The corresponding noise equivalent power is achieved as low as 0.3 fW/Hz[MATH], which indicates at least a ten-fold improvement over previous results. Notably, the involved single-frequency pumping would facilitate high-fidelity spectral mapping, which is particularly attractive for high-precision MIR upconversion spectroscopy in photon-starved scenarios.
tldr: This paper presents a mid-infrared upconversion detection system using external-cavity pump enhancement to achieve high sensitivity and low noise.
motivation: High-performance passive MIR sensing is challenging due to the need for high-power continuous-wave pumping; the authors aim to improve conversion efficiency and reduce noise.
method: They use a low-loss optical cavity to enhance a single-longitudinal-mode pump at 1064 nm by a factor of 36, achieving intra-cavity average power of 55 W.
result: Peak conversion efficiency of 22% and noise equivalent power as low as 0.3 fW/Hz^0.5, a ten-fold improvement over previous results.
conclusion: The system enables high-fidelity spectral mapping for high-precision MIR upconversion spectroscopy in photon-starved scenarios.

title: Single-photon Time-stretch Infrared Spectroscopy
authors: Ben Sun, Kun Huang, Huijie Ma, Jianan Fang, Tingting Zheng, Yongyuan Chu, Hairun Guo, Yan Liang, E Wu, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensitive mid-infrared (MIR) spectroscopy is highly demanded in various fields ranging from industrial inspection, biomedical diagnosis to astronomical observation. However, the detection sensitivity of conventional MIR spectrometers has been severely limited by excessive noises for existing infrared sensors, which hinders widespread use in photon-scarce scenarios. Here, we devise and implement a broadband MIR single-photon time-stretch spectrometer based on high-fidelity spectral upconversion and time-correlated coincidence counting. Specifically, a nanophotonic supercontinuum illumination covering 2.4-4.2 [MATH]m is nonlinearly converted to the near-infrared band, where low-loss single-mode fiber and high-performance silicon detector can be leveraged to facilitate dispersive operation and sensitive detection, respectively. The arrival time for the dispersed upconversion photons is precisely registered with a low-timing-jitter photon counter, which enables us to obtain a high spectral resolution about 0.5 cm[MATH] under a low-light-level illumination down to 0.14 photons/nm/pulse. In comparison to previous MIR upconversion spectrometers, the presented time-stretch architecture favors single-pixel simplicity and high-throughput acquisition for the single-photon spectral measurement. The achieved MIR spectroscopic features of broadband spectral coverage, sub-wavenumber resolution, single-photon sensitivity, and room-temperature operation would stimulate immediate applications in material and life sciences.
tldr: This paper presents a single-photon time-stretch infrared spectrometer using spectral upconversion and coincidence counting for sensitive mid-infrared spectroscopy.
motivation: Conventional MIR spectrometers suffer from noise and limited sensitivity, hindering use in photon-scarce scenarios. The authors aim to achieve broadband, high-resolution MIR spectroscopy at the single-photon level.
method: A nanophotonic supercontinuum (2.4-4.2 μm) is upconverted to near-infrared via nonlinear conversion, then dispersed in single-mode fiber and detected with a low-timing-jitter silicon photon counter using time-correlated coincidence counting.
result: The spectrometer achieves a spectral resolution of ~0.5 cm⁻¹ under illumination as low as 0.14 photons/nm/pulse, with broadband coverage and single-photon sensitivity.
conclusion: The demonstrated single-photon time-stretch MIR spectrometer offers high sensitivity, resolution, and room-temperature operation, promising applications in material and life sciences.

title: Wide-field Mid-infrared Hyperspectral Imaging Beyond Video Rate
authors: Jianan Fang, Kun Huang, Ruiyang Qin, Yan Liang, E Wu, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mid-infrared hyperspectral imaging has become an indispensable tool to spatially resolve chemical information in a wide variety of samples. However, acquiring three-dimensional data cubes is typically time-consuming due to the limited speed of raster scanning or wavelength tuning, which impedes real-time visualization with high spatial definition across broad spectral bands. Here, we devise and implement a high-speed, wide-field mid-infrared hyperspectral imaging system relying on broadband parametric upconversion of high-brightness supercontinuum illumination at the Fourier plane. The upconverted replica is spectrally decomposed by a rapid acousto-optic tunable filter, which records high-definition monochromatic images at a frame rate of 10 kHz based on a megapixel silicon camera. Consequently, the hyperspectral imager allows us to acquire 100 spectral bands over 2600-4085 cm[MATH] in 10 ms, corresponding to a refreshing rate of 100 Hz. Moreover, the angular dependence of phase matching in the image upconversion is leveraged to realize snapshot operation with spatial multiplexing for multiple spectral channels, which may further boost the spectral imaging rate. The high acquisition rate, wide-field operation, and broadband spectral coverage could open new possibilities for high-throughput characterization of transient processes in material and life sciences.
tldr: This paper presents a high-speed, wide-field mid-infrared hyperspectral imaging system using parametric upconversion and acousto-optic filtering, achieving 100 spectral bands at 100 Hz.
motivation: To overcome the slow acquisition speed of conventional mid-infrared hyperspectral imaging, enabling real-time visualization of transient processes.
method: Broadband parametric upconversion of supercontinuum illumination at the Fourier plane, followed by spectral decomposition with a rapid acousto-optic tunable filter and detection by a megapixel silicon camera.
result: The system records 100 spectral bands over 2600-4085 cm⁻¹ in 10 ms (100 Hz refresh rate) with 10 kHz frame rate per monochromatic image.
conclusion: The high acquisition rate and wide-field operation could enable high-throughput characterization of transient processes in material and life sciences.

title: Scalable All-Optical Fibre-Mode Data Transmission With Profiles-Preserved Decoding
authors: Rundong Fan, Yamin Zheng, Pei Li, Xixiao Cao, Haoyang Wu, Zheng Cai, Lei Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical fibres are the primary medium for optical signal transmission, and their guided modes provide a high-dimensional basis for modal-domain information encoding. However, conventional demultiplexing approaches typically convert fibre modes into fundamental Gaussian modes and require repeated mode conversions, while existing profiles-preserved methods are generally restricted to fewer than three modes. High-quality fibre-mode data transmission therefore requires a scalable all-optical decoder capable of separating strongly overlapping modal channels while preserving their intrinsic spatial profiles. Here, we establish a scalable profiles-preserved all-optical decoding method for high-dimensional fibre-mode data transmission. By introducing a microlens-array-assisted decoding architecture with channel-dependent spherical phase compensation, the proposed method accommodates mode-dependent effective focal-length variations, enabling scalable modal-channel separation while preserving high-quality modal profiles at the output plane. Experimentally, the optical decoder resolved fields containing eight fibre modes, achieving a mode fidelity exceeding 0.72, a worst-channel crosstalk of [MATH] and a mean non-target crosstalk of [MATH], while reconstructing the relative modal weights with an error below 0.1. Semantic transmission experiments using digits and Chinese characters further demonstrated effective recovery of the encoded information from the decoded modal signals. We expect this work to provide a scalable route towards high-dimensional all-optical fibre-mode data transmission.
tldr: This paper presents a scalable all-optical decoder for high-dimensional fibre-mode data transmission using a microlens-array-assisted architecture with spherical phase compensation.
motivation: Conventional demultiplexing methods require repeated mode conversions and are limited to few modes, hindering scalable high-dimensional fibre-mode data transmission.
method: A microlens-array-assisted decoding architecture with channel-dependent spherical phase compensation is introduced to separate modal channels while preserving their spatial profiles.
result: The decoder resolved eight fibre modes with mode fidelity >0.72, worst-channel crosstalk of -10.2 dB, mean non-target crosstalk of -14.3 dB, and modal weight reconstruction error <0.1.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route towards high-dimensional all-optical fibre-mode data transmission, with potential applications in optical communications.

title: Connection Factorization In Constrained Quantum Mechanics
authors: A. Nuramatov
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate constrained quantum motion on curves and surfaces using connection factorization methods. We show that Laplace operators admit an exact half-connection factorization generated by connection one-forms. The first-order part of the Laplacian is identified with the Darboux rotational connection of the orthogonal frame. Elimination of this rotational connection naturally produces quadratic geometric invariants analogous to supersymmetric Riccati potentials. Using orthonormal moving frames, we derive effective geometric contributions for planar curves, spatial curves, and embedded surfaces. We further analyze Dirac reductions using structure equations and show that for Fermi-type reductions the scalar Jensen--Koppe--da Costa contribution is cancelled in the reduced Dirac sector, leaving a residual first-order spinorial derivative structure. The resulting framework suggests the existence of hidden nilpotent covariant differential complexes naturally generated by geometric connection structures.
tldr: This paper studies constrained quantum motion on curves and surfaces using connection factorization, deriving geometric invariants and Dirac reductions.
motivation: To understand the geometric structure of quantum mechanics on curved manifolds and to develop factorization methods for Laplace operators.
method: Connection factorization of Laplace operators using orthonormal moving frames and Darboux rotational connections, with analysis of Dirac reductions.
result: Laplace operators admit half-connection factorization; elimination of rotational connection yields quadratic geometric invariants; Fermi-type reductions cancel scalar contributions leaving spinorial derivative structure.
conclusion: The framework suggests hidden nilpotent covariant differential complexes generated by geometric connections, with potential applications in constrained quantum systems.

title: Saddle Networks: Structure-Preserving Architectures For Convex-Concave Functions
authors: Xavier Warin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Saddle-point models arise throughout optimization, optimal transport, robust learning, and control. In many applications, the relevant function f(x,y) is convex in x and concave in y, and preserving this geometry is essential for obtaining tractable min--max formulations and reliable certificates. We introduce a structured separable decomposition that preserves the convex-concave geometry and prove a complete one-dimensional approximation theorem under a mixed Monge-type convexity condition. We then describe practical saddle network architectures that preserve convexity in x and concavity in y by construction. The proposed architectures require only convexity-preserving neural networks, together with simple output transformations enforcing sign and concavity constraints. Finally, we report numerical benchmarks in dimension 1 and 5, showing that the proposed saddle networks achieve high accuracy on smooth, nonsmooth, and high-rank convex--concave test functions.
tldr: This paper introduces neural network architectures that preserve convex-concave geometry for saddle-point problems, with applications in optimization and robust learning.
motivation: Saddle-point problems are common in optimization and machine learning, but standard neural networks do not preserve the convex-concave structure needed for tractable min-max formulations.
method: The authors propose a separable decomposition and use convexity-preserving neural networks with output transformations to enforce sign and concavity constraints, creating saddle network architectures.
result: The proposed saddle networks achieve high accuracy on smooth, nonsmooth, and high-rank convex-concave test functions in dimensions 1 and 5.
conclusion: The work provides a practical way to embed convex-concave geometry into neural networks, with potential applications in optimization and robust learning, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Existence Of Gibbs Measures For Sequences Of Continuous Functions
authors: Yuki Yayama
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an equivalent condition for the existence of invariant Gibbs measures for sequences of continuous functions on one-sided subshifts and, more generally, for the existence of Gibbs measures. These extend the results of Kim [6] and Baker and Ghenciu [2], respectively, to sequences of continuous functions on one-sided subshifts. In particular, we characterize the existence of invariant Gibbs measures for subadditive sequences. For superadditive sequences on subshifts with the strong specification property, such a characterization gives an equivalent condition for the uniqueness of invariant ergodic Gibbs measures. We apply these results to study some problems in the theory of relative pressure and relative equilibrium states.
tldr: This paper studies the existence of Gibbs measures for sequences of continuous functions on one-sided subshifts, extending previous results to subadditive and superadditive sequences.
motivation: To generalize known conditions for the existence of invariant Gibbs measures to sequences of continuous functions, and to characterize uniqueness for superadditive sequences under strong specification.
method: The authors use thermodynamic formalism and symbolic dynamics, analyzing subadditive and superadditive sequences on one-sided subshifts with the strong specification property.
result: They provide an equivalent condition for the existence of invariant Gibbs measures for subadditive sequences, and for superadditive sequences under strong specification, this condition also implies uniqueness of invariant ergodic Gibbs measures.
conclusion: The results extend prior work and have applications to relative pressure and relative equilibrium states, but the paper is purely mathematical and not directly connected to the user's research interests.

title: Algorithm To Check Maximum Likelihood Estimate Existence For Integrated Pca
authors: Dmitri Shmelkin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Being encouraged by [AKRS] that provides an amazing bridge between Statistics and Invariant Theory, and especially by [FM], where quiver semi-invariant techniques apply to verify the existence of MLE for a recent iPCA model, we provide an enhancement to [FM]. Our Theorem 5.2 yields necessary and sufficient conditions for MLE to exist generically for any dimension vector. The conditions can be easily checked with our software [T] based on Derksen-Weyman algorithm and simplifying the application for statistics practitioners and non-specialists in quivers. For those deep in quiver Representation Theory, Theorem 5.2 relates the MLE existence to the local semi-simplicity of representations as introduced in [Sh07]. We also hope that our elementary and short text can serve for the experts in both domains as a warm start in a new category.
tldr: This paper presents an algorithm to check the existence of maximum likelihood estimates for integrated PCA using quiver representation theory.
motivation: To extend previous work linking statistics and invariant theory, specifically to provide necessary and sufficient conditions for MLE existence in iPCA models.
method: The authors use quiver semi-invariant techniques and the Derksen-Weyman algorithm to derive conditions for generic MLE existence.
result: Theorem 5.2 gives necessary and sufficient conditions for MLE existence for any dimension vector, which can be checked with provided software.
conclusion: The work simplifies application for statisticians and offers a bridge between statistics and quiver representation theory, with potential for further cross-domain research.

title: Manifold-based Algorithms For The Hadamard Decomposition
authors: Nicolas Gillis, Subhayan Saha, Stefano Sicilia, Arnaud Vandaele
abstract: ArXiv:2605.28980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a matrix [MATH], and two ranks [MATH] and [MATH], the Hadamard decomposition (HD) looks for two low-rank matrices, [MATH] of rank [MATH] and [MATH] of rank [MATH], both of the same size as [MATH], such that [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hadamard (element-wise) product. In most cases, HD is more expressive than standard low-rank approximations such as the truncated singular value decomposition (TSVD), as it can represent higher-rank matrices with the same number of parameters; this is because the rank of [MATH] is generically equal to [MATH]. In this paper, we first present some theoretical insights for HD, in particular a useful reformulation [MATH] where [MATH] and [MATH] have [MATH] columns and belong to certain manifolds. These allow us to develop three new algorithms for computing HD. The first one uses the representation [MATH] and relies on the Manopt toolbox. The other two rely on the reformulation [MATH]: one is a block projected gradient method, and the other is a manifold-based gradient descent algorithm that does not require projection onto the feasible set. The last two algorithms are particularly effective for handling large sparse data. We also propose new initializations that allow us to improve the accuracy of the HD. We compare our algorithms and initialization strategies with the TSVD and with the state of the art. Numerical results show that the new methods are efficient and competitive on both synthetic and real data.
tldr: This paper develops manifold-based algorithms for the Hadamard decomposition of a matrix into two low-rank factors.
motivation: The Hadamard decomposition is more expressive than standard low-rank approximations, but existing algorithms are limited. The authors aim to provide efficient and scalable methods.
method: Three algorithms are proposed: one using Manopt toolbox on a reformulation, a block projected gradient method, and a manifold-based gradient descent without projection. New initialization strategies are also introduced.
result: The new algorithms are competitive with state-of-the-art on synthetic and real data, especially for large sparse matrices.
conclusion: The work advances numerical methods for Hadamard decomposition, with potential applications in data analysis and machine learning.

title: A Minimal Bifurcation Model Of Load Imbalance In A Softmax Mixture-of-Experts Router
authors: O. M. Kiselev
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a minimal dynamical model of adaptive softmax routing for a two-expert Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer. The model is obtained as a mean-field limit of a discrete reinforcement rule: the selected expert receives a small score increment, while all scores undergo regularizing decay. In the symmetric case the limiting system has a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation: for weak feedback there is a unique stable balanced state, whereas above a critical feedback strength two stable asymmetric states appear. When an external asymmetry is added, the pitchfork unfolds into a pair of fold bifurcations forming a cusp in the control-parameter plane. We derive exact parametric equations for the bifurcation set and the local normal form of the cusp catastrophe. Numerical experiments connect this picture to empirical expert load, a small trainable MoE model, hard top-1 PyTorch routing, and a small classification experiment on digits. The results provide a controlled low-dimensional mechanism for abrupt transitions to load imbalance in adaptive MoE routers.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal dynamical model of load imbalance in a softmax mixture-of-experts router, analyzing bifurcations and cusp catastrophes.
motivation: To understand abrupt transitions to load imbalance in adaptive MoE routers, which is a practical issue in machine learning.
method: Derives a mean-field limit of a discrete reinforcement rule, analyzes bifurcations (pitchfork and cusp) analytically, and validates with numerical experiments on small MoE models.
result: Identifies supercritical pitchfork bifurcation in symmetric case and cusp catastrophe with asymmetry; exact parametric equations for bifurcation set derived.
conclusion: Provides a low-dimensional mechanism for load imbalance, but implications for quantum or thermodynamic systems are not discussed.

title: Multifidelity Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
authors: Karen Willcox Nicole Aretz
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a multifidelity formulation that reduces the computational cost of the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of a high-fidelity model by leveraging data from cheaper, lower-fidelity models. POD is a prevalent technique for extracting a low-dimensional basis from training data to achieve subsequent dimension reduction or reduced-order modeling. In scientific and engineering applications, the training data are typically numerical snapshot solutions of a high-fidelity model, and computation of a sufficiently rich snapshot set can be prohibitively expensive, especially when sampling over a high-dimensional parameter space. Insufficient snapshot training data risks overfitting and poor generalizability of the POD basis to outside the training regime. Our multifidelity POD (MFPOD) formulation reallocates computational budget to cheaper, low-fidelity models that can be sampled more extensively. MFPOD then weights high- and low-fidelity snapshot data via a control-variate formulation to guarantee an unbiased estimate of the expected high-fidelity least-squares projection error. The MFPOD subspace is chosen to minimize the estimate of this projection error, and converges in probability to the same subspace as single-fidelity POD in the limit of an arbitrarily large budget. For restrictive computational budgets, the MFPOD cost function has (under some assumptions) lower variance than the POD cost function, which makes the MFPOD subspace more robust against variations in the training data and thus less prone to overfitting. For a numerical example modeling the velocity of the Pine Island glacier, MFPOD achieves the same accuracy as single-fidelity POD with an order of magnitude reduction in the offline computational cost of snapshot generation.
tldr: This paper introduces a multifidelity proper orthogonal decomposition method that reduces computational cost by leveraging cheaper low-fidelity models.
motivation: Computing high-fidelity snapshot sets for POD can be prohibitively expensive, especially in high-dimensional parameter spaces, leading to overfitting and poor generalization.
method: The authors propose a multifidelity POD (MFPOD) that reallocates computational budget to low-fidelity models, weighting high- and low-fidelity data via a control-variate formulation to produce an unbiased estimate of the projection error.
result: MFPOD converges in probability to the same subspace as single-fidelity POD with sufficient budget, and for limited budgets it exhibits lower variance, reducing overfitting. A numerical example on Pine Island glacier velocity modeling shows an order-of-magnitude reduction in offline computational cost.
conclusion: MFPOD offers a cost-effective alternative to standard POD for large-scale simulations, with potential applications in scientific computing and engineering.

title: The Weak Galerkin Method For A Class Of Gross-Pitaevskii Type Eigenvalue Problems
authors: Qilong Zhai Wei Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper aims to employ the weak Galerkin method to solve a class of nonlinear eigenvalue problems. We proved the weak Galerkin scheme produces lower bound for the energy. Moreover, by the post-processing technique, we obtain lower bound for the ground state eigenvalue. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to validate the theoretical analysis.
tldr: This paper applies the weak Galerkin method to compute lower bounds for eigenvalues of Gross-Pitaevskii type nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
motivation: To develop a numerical method that provides guaranteed lower bounds for eigenvalues in nonlinear eigenvalue problems, which is important for validating numerical simulations.
method: The weak Galerkin finite element method is employed, and a post-processing technique is used to obtain lower bounds for the ground state eigenvalue.
result: The weak Galerkin scheme produces lower bounds for the energy, and numerical experiments confirm the theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The method offers a reliable way to compute lower eigenvalue bounds for nonlinear problems, with potential extensions to other eigenvalue problems.

title: Restarted Accelerated Primal-Dual Algorithms With Adaptive Stepsizes For Nonlinear Conic Constrained Convex Optimization
authors: Jinxin Wang Necdet Serhat Aybat
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose restarted accelerated primal-dual algorithms with (non-monotone) backtracking (rAPDB) for convex nonlinear conic programs, with quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQPs) as a special case. Unlike linear and quadratic programs, these problems give rise to convex-concave minimax reformulations with non-bilinear coupling terms; therefore, the existing primal-dual methods for bilinear couplings are not applicable. To address this challenge, we build on the accelerated primal-dual method with adaptive stepsize search -- as it adapts to the local curvature -- and develop both fixed-frequency and adaptive restart schemes, incorporating both monotone and non-monotone adaptive step-size search strategies. The resulting algorithms require only first-order information and matrix-vector products, making them suitable for large-scale and GPU-accelerated implementation. Under metric subregularity of the KKT mapping, we prove a quadratic growth property for a self-centered smoothed duality gap and establish global linear convergence of the proposed restarted methods. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the metric subregularity holds even for general nonconvex problems over convex polyhedral cones. These results are new and may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments on random QCQPs and kernel matrix learning instances show that the proposed methods, especially with non-monotone adaptive stepsizes and GPU acceleration, achieve strong practical performance.
tldr: This paper develops restarted accelerated primal-dual algorithms with adaptive stepsizes for nonlinear conic convex optimization, focusing on QCQPs and kernel matrix learning.
motivation: Existing primal-dual methods for bilinear couplings cannot handle convex-concave minimax reformulations with non-bilinear coupling terms arising in nonlinear conic programs.
method: The authors build on accelerated primal-dual methods with adaptive stepsize search, incorporating fixed-frequency and adaptive restart schemes with monotone and non-monotone backtracking.
result: Global linear convergence is proved under metric subregularity of the KKT mapping, and sufficient conditions for metric subregularity are established for nonconvex problems over convex polyhedral cones.
conclusion: The proposed methods achieve strong practical performance on random QCQPs and kernel matrix learning, especially with non-monotone adaptive stepsizes and GPU acceleration.

title: Global Optimization Of Quadratic Root-difference Minimization Under Elliptic Annulus Constraints
authors: Yong Xia Meijia Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the nonconvex quadratic root-difference minimization under elliptic annulus constraints {\rm (QR)}. We first establish the Annulus Brickman theorem and equivalently reformulate {\rm (QR)} as a 2-dimensional convex problem {\rm (HP)} with hidden variables. We employ the Frank-Wolfe algorithm to globally solve {\rm (HP)}. A key finding is that the solutions of the Frank-Wolfe subproblems, which are traditionally viewed as mere auxiliary updates, are proven to be [MATH]-approximate solutions of the original problem {\rm (QR)}. This transforms an algorithmic by-product into the primary output and completely bypasses the need to solve the computationally expensive quadratic system required for solution recovery. Leveraging this recovery-free property, we develop the efficient Iterative Minimum Generalized Eigenpair (IMGE) algorithm for globally solving {\rm (QR)}. Numerical experiments confirm that IMGE converges rapidly and significantly outperforms conventional methods, especially for large-scale problems.
tldr: This paper presents a global optimization algorithm for a nonconvex quadratic root-difference minimization problem under elliptic annulus constraints, with no apparent connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The research addresses a challenging nonconvex optimization problem that arises in certain engineering or applied mathematics contexts, aiming to develop an efficient global solution method.
method: The authors reformulate the problem as a 2D convex problem using an Annulus Brickman theorem, then apply the Frank-Wolfe algorithm. They prove that the subproblem solutions are approximate solutions of the original problem, leading to a recovery-free algorithm called Iterative Minimum Generalized Eigenpair (IMGE).
result: The IMGE algorithm converges rapidly and outperforms conventional methods, especially for large-scale problems, by avoiding expensive quadratic system recovery.
conclusion: The work provides a novel optimization technique for a specific class of problems, but its relevance to quantum computing, condensed matter physics, or machine learning is not evident.

title: On Subspace-constrained Preconditioning For Randomized Iterative Methods
authors: Yonghan Sun, Hou-Duo Qi, Deren Han, Jiaxin Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we further investigate and refine the subspace-constrained preconditioning technique to enhance the theoretical and numerical convergence properties of randomized iterative methods for solving linear systems. In particular, we design a QR-like factorization that transforms the original linear system into an equivalent block-orthogonal form, thus avoiding the full-rank assumptions adopted in existing work. Moreover, this reformulation reduces the problem to solving a smaller linear system with a favorable singular value distribution, provided an appropriate initial point is employed. The proposed framework can be implemented implicitly within the iteration and does not require explicitly constructing either a preconditioner matrix or a preconditioned linear system, which eliminates the prohibitive cost of forming a fully preconditioned system. Furthermore, we construct orthogonalized search directions from stochastic gradients and develop accelerated variants of the framework. We prove that the proposed algorithmic framework converges linearly in expectation. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of the proposed preconditioning strategy.
tldr: This paper develops a subspace-constrained preconditioning technique for randomized iterative methods to solve linear systems, improving convergence without explicit preconditioner construction.
motivation: To enhance the convergence of randomized iterative methods for linear systems by designing a preconditioning technique that avoids full-rank assumptions and reduces computational cost.
method: The authors propose a QR-like factorization to transform the linear system into a block-orthogonal form, enabling a smaller system with better singular value distribution. They also construct orthogonalized search directions from stochastic gradients and develop accelerated variants.
result: The proposed framework converges linearly in expectation, and numerical experiments demonstrate improved performance over existing methods.
conclusion: The subspace-constrained preconditioning offers an efficient way to accelerate randomized iterative methods without explicit preconditioner construction, with potential for further acceleration and application to other iterative algorithms.

title: High-order Time Splitting Methods For The Nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii Equation
authors: Roberto Ben, Agust\'in Besteiro, Diego Rial
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a high-order numerical methodology for computing the ground state and time evolution of the two-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation with harmonic trapping potential. The ground state is obtained by combining normalized gradient flow with time-splitting schemes featuring strictly positive coefficients, which makes them suitable for both dissipative and Hamiltonian regimes and avoids the negative time steps required by classical symplectic methods. The computational cost of these methods grows quadratically with the order, in contrast to the exponential growth of symplectic alternatives. Numerical benchmarks assess ground state convergence under different initializations, long-time preservation of mass and Hamiltonian energy for varying mass constraints, and the cost-accuracy trade-off for orders q = 2, 4,..., 14.
tldr: This paper develops high-order time-splitting methods for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, focusing on numerical efficiency and accuracy for ground state and time evolution.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of classical symplectic methods that require negative time steps and have exponential cost scaling with order.
method: Combines normalized gradient flow with time-splitting schemes using strictly positive coefficients, achieving high order with quadratic cost scaling.
result: Demonstrates convergence, long-time preservation of mass and energy, and favorable cost-accuracy trade-off for orders up to 14.
conclusion: The proposed methods are efficient and accurate for simulating Bose-Einstein condensates, with potential extensions to other nonlinear PDEs.

title: Kernel-based Potential Mean-field Games With Unbiased Random Fourier $U$-statistics
authors: Yumiharu Nakano
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the subclass of potential mean-field games in which the running interaction cost and the terminal target cost are both expressed through reproducing-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) penalties, and develop a computational framework that exploits this kernel structure. Both costs are estimated from finite-sample empirical distributions using a random Fourier U-statistic representation that is unbiased and has linear cost in the batch size. The drift of the controlled diffusion is parametrized by a neural network and trained via stochastic gradient descent. For this subclass we prove a sample-level almost-sure convergence theorem and an explicit almost-sure rate of convergence, under coupled rate conditions on the penalty parameter, the random-feature count, the sample size, and the optimization tolerance. The framework includes the kernel-MMD-penalty Schr\"odinger bridge problem as the special case of a vanishing interaction cost. Numerical experiments illustrate the method on the Schr\"odinger bridge problem in dimensions up to one hundred, and on an electric vehicle charging coordination problem with per-vehicle physical heterogeneity, where an aggregate-demand congestion cost represents price-feedback competition at the population level and the terminal MMD penalty shapes the state-of-charge distribution at the deadline.
tldr: This paper develops a computational framework for potential mean-field games with kernel-based MMD penalties using unbiased random Fourier U-statistics.
motivation: To efficiently solve mean-field games with interaction and terminal costs expressed as maximum mean discrepancy penalties, which arise in applications like Schrödinger bridges and EV charging coordination.
method: The costs are estimated via unbiased random Fourier U-statistics with linear batch cost; the drift is parametrized by a neural network and trained via stochastic gradient descent.
result: Proved almost-sure convergence and explicit rate under coupled conditions on penalty, feature count, sample size, and optimization tolerance; demonstrated on high-dimensional Schrödinger bridge and EV charging problems.
conclusion: The framework provides a scalable and theoretically grounded approach for kernel-MMD-penalized mean-field games, with potential extensions to other MMD-based problems.

title: Linear Stability Analysis Of The Lloyd Algorithm On A Circle
authors: Silpi Saha, Sangita Jha, Mrinal Kanti Roychowdhury
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lloyd algorithm is the standard iterative method for computing quantizers and codebooks in source coding and vector quantization. In this article, we study the dynamical and stability properties of the Lloyd map on the unit circle [MATH] using von Mises distributions. We construct the Lloyd iteration as a discrete dynamical system on the configuration space of ordered point sets modulo rotational symmetry. Also, we study the rotational equivarience of the Lloyd map. Further, we derive an explicit representation of the Jacobian matrix and prove that it possesses a circulant structure for the equally spaced configuration. Also, we study the bifurcation characteristics based on Lloyd map analysis. In the end, we provide the numerical algorithms for stability diagrams, Lyapunov spectrum estimation, and residue analysis, purely for empirical visualization. Our results provide a dynamical systems framework for Lloyd quantization on [MATH] for studying stability properties.
tldr: This paper analyzes the linear stability of the Lloyd algorithm on a circle using von Mises distributions, focusing on dynamical systems and bifurcation analysis.
motivation: To understand the stability and dynamics of the Lloyd algorithm, which is used for quantization, specifically on a circle geometry.
method: Constructs the Lloyd iteration as a discrete dynamical system, derives the Jacobian matrix with circulant structure for equally spaced configurations, and performs bifurcation analysis and numerical simulations.
result: Provides explicit Jacobian representation, proves circulant structure, and studies stability diagrams, Lyapunov spectra, and residue analysis.
conclusion: Offers a dynamical systems framework for Lloyd quantization on a circle, with implications for understanding stability properties of the algorithm.

title: The Stein-Chen Method And A Law Of Small Numbers In Riesz Spaces
authors: Wen-Chi Kuo, Nigel Musara, Bruce A. Watson
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Martingales, Markov processes and Laws of Large Numbers have been well studied in the Riesz space (vector lattice) setting. There has, however, been no attention given in the Riesz space setting to Laws of Small Numbers or to the so called Stein-Chen method. Here we adapt the Stein-Chen method to the Riesz space setting and hence give a conditional Laws of Small Numbers for Bernoulli processes in Riesz spaces. This requires extensive use of functional calculus and the associated f-algebra structure.
tldr: This paper extends the Stein-Chen method and law of small numbers to Riesz spaces, a purely mathematical framework with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To fill a gap in Riesz space theory by developing conditional laws of small numbers and the Stein-Chen method, which had not been studied in this abstract setting.
method: The authors adapt the Stein-Chen method to Riesz spaces using functional calculus and the f-algebra structure, proving a conditional law of small numbers for Bernoulli processes.
result: A conditional law of small numbers for Bernoulli processes in Riesz spaces is established, generalizing classical results to a more abstract algebraic framework.
conclusion: The work contributes to Riesz space theory but has no immediate applications to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or condensed matter physics.

title: Frame Constructions Associated With Operator Orbits
authors: Jonathan R. Partington Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez
abstract: ArXiv:2605.29671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies frames in Hilbert spaces generated by the orbits of (in)-finitely many vectors under a single operator, presenting new results on multiplication operators and operators composed of Jordan blocks, which generalizes existing results of Cabrelli, Molter, Paternostro and Philipp by means of techniques which deal with weighted interpolation, weighted composition operators, and Beurling--Lax theory related to shifts of infinity multiplicity.
